## Question 1 (E.1a)

Multiply the likelihood by the prior and collect the powers of each factor:
$$\theta_1^{x_1} \theta_2^{x_2} (1 - \theta_1 - \theta_2)^{x_3} \cdot
  \theta_1^{\delta_1 - 1} \theta_2^{\delta_2 - 1} (1 - \theta_1 - \theta_2)^{\delta_3 - 1}
  = \theta_1^{e_1 - 1}\, \theta_2^{e_2 - 1}\, (1 - \theta_1 - \theta_2)^{e_3 - 1}$$

What are $e_1$, $e_2$ and $e_3$?

## Question 2 (E.1b)

Let $a_1 = x_1 + \delta_1$, $b = x_3 + \delta_3$ and $s = 1 - \theta_2$.
Keeping only the factors with $\theta_1$,
$\pi(\theta_1 \mid \theta_2, x) \propto \theta_1^{a_1 - 1} (s - \theta_1)^{b - 1}$
for $0 < \theta_1 < s$. For $B \sim \text{Beta}(a_1, b)$, the density of $sB$ is
$$\frac{1}{s} f_B\!\left(\frac{\theta_1}{s}\right) \propto
  \left(\frac{\theta_1}{s}\right)^{a_1 - 1} \left(1 - \frac{\theta_1}{s}\right)^{b - 1}
  \propto \text{(blank)}$$

What goes in the blank, dropping factors without $\theta_1$?

**Answer:**

## Question 3 (E.2)

Fill in the blanks, with every $\delta_i = 1$. The last two lines print the
posterior means, the 95% intervals and $P(\theta_1/\theta_2 > 2 \mid x)$.

```{r e2}
gibbs <- function(k, t1 = 1/3, t2 = 1/3) {
  chain <- matrix(0, k, 2, dimnames = list(NULL, c("theta1", "theta2")))
  for (i in 1:k) {
    t1 <- (1 - t2) * rbeta(1, x1 + 1, x3 + 1)
    t2 <- ________ * rbeta(1, ________, ________)
    chain[i, ] <- c(t1, t2)
  }
  chain
}
chain <- gibbs(5000)
matplot(chain, type = "l", lty = 1)          # trace plot
post <- chain[-(1:1000), ]
post <- cbind(post, theta3 = 1 - post[, "theta1"] - post[, "theta2"])
rbind(mean = colMeans(post), apply(post, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975)))
mean(post[, "theta1"] / post[, "theta2"] > 2)
```

## Question 5 (C.2b)

Back to Part C. Fill in the blank.

**Note.** Accept-reject and importance resampling both avoid the normalizing
constant $k$ in $f = k\,f^*$. Accept-reject only needs $c\,g \ge f^*$, and
the $k$s cancel in the ratio in its proof. Importance resampling normalizes
the weights, and $k$ cancels there. The video writes this constant as $c$.
That $c$ is not the accept-reject envelope constant.

```{r c2b}
y2 <- runif(10000)
w <- fstar(y2) / sum(fstar(y2))
sir <- sample(y2, 5000, replace = TRUE, prob = ____)
mean(sir)
```
